Hi Ana — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick answer up front and then details below.

Short options:
1) Wire USD to our USD collection account (preferred if you want no FX on our side).
2) Wire GBP to our GBP collection account — bank will convert to USD; this route can trigger intermediary/correspondent fees depending on your sending bank’s chain.

We generally ask for gross/beneficiary-receives-full where possible; if the payment arrives short we will issue a shortfall invoice. Below are explicit instruction snippets your payments desk can paste into their banking system. I'm attaching our current wire stub (redwood_wire_instructions_v2.pdf).

---- Option A — USD (no conversion by our bank):
Remit to: Redwood Inference Ltd — USD Collection
Account: GB00REDW00000012345678
Bank: Oak & Pine Bank, New York
SWIFT: OPNBUS33
Reference: INV 5372 / Globex PO 889
Instruction: Sender to cover all correspondent/intermediary fees ("OUR").

---- Option B — GBP (you prefer to pay in GBP):
Remit to: Redwood Inference Ltd — GBP Collection
Account: GB11REDW00000087654321
Bank: Redwood UK Clearing (via correspondent chain)
SWIFT: REDWGB2L
Reference: INV 5372 / Globex PO 889
Instruction options (choose one):
  - Sender pays all fees (OUR) — recommended if you want Redwood to receive full invoice amount.
  - Beneficiary pays fees (BEN) — if selected, the net credited amount may be short; Redwood will invoice any shortfall.

Note on intermediary fees: depending on the sending bank and routing, a correspondent bank may deduct a fee before the funds reach our GBP account. If you choose OUR, the sending bank will attempt to debit fees from your account and the beneficiary receives full amount. If you choose BEN, the sending bank may transmit a lower amount and we will invoice the shortfall.

VAT / invoice supporting fields:
- Please include the invoice number and our VAT ID on the remittance.
- We can provide a sample invoice with a clearly separate VAT line for your reclaim — attaching sample_invoice_5372.pdf. Laura, can you confirm this satisfies UK VAT reclaim conventions?

Let me know which option you want us to expect and we’ll confirm the exact account routing details if you need a specific correspondent chain listed.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Tom / Ana — thanks. Below are two paste-in blocks (copy/paste into Barclays or your aggregator). I also include our recommendation at the end.

--- PASTE BLOCK: OPTION A (USD wire - preferred for predictable receipt) ---
Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd
Account (USD): GB00REDW00000012345678
Bank: Oak & Pine Bank, New York
SWIFT: OPNBUS33
Reference: INV 5372 / GLOBEX PO 889
Charges: OUR

--- PASTE BLOCK: OPTION B (GBP wire to GBP collection account) ---
Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd
Account (GBP): GB11REDW00000087654321
Bank: Redwood UK Clearing (via correspondent chain)
SWIFT: REDWGB2L
Reference: INV 5372 / GLOBEX PO 889
Charges: OUR (if you want Redwood to receive full amount)

Notes on FX spread and cost:
- If you send USD (Option A) there is no FX spread applied by our bank. Your bank will debit your GBP account and convert to USD before sending, or you can fund USD directly from a USD pool — that is up to your treasury.
- If you send GBP (Option B) to our GBP account, our GBP collection bank will convert to USD when moving funds into our USD operations. The FX spread is typically applied by the converting bank in that chain. If you select OUR, you cover intermediary/correspondent fees but not necessarily the FX spread charged by a converting bank.

Recommendation: For minimizing total cost and operational friction, Option A (USD wire) usually wins if your treasury can fund a USD payment. If your operations policy forces GBP, choose Option B with Charges: OUR so that Redwood receives the full invoiced amount and we avoid shortfall reconciliation.

I have attached a short text stub you can provide to Barclays as well (redwood_wire_stub.txt) and a sample invoice with VAT line (sample_invoice_5372.pdf). We'll monitor and notify when funds settle.

Best,
Hannah
